correctness.rationale: The telescoping Cauchy-dual moment formula is exact. Rational 2x2 and 3x3 determinant factorizations were independently symbolically reproduced. For all a>0 and y>=0 the u-cubic has one real positive root since its discriminant is negative, reducing infinitely many shifted 3x3 tests to n=0. For u>=4 the y-cubic is strictly decreasing, giving one sharp root. Exact substitution proves this root lies below the 2x2 threshold, and a Schur complement covers singular equality. The signed Hausdorff density is integrable and necessarily changes sign for b>0, proving non-subnormality through compact-interval moment uniqueness. Finite tests support, not replace, the all-parameter argument.

originality.rationale: The exact same quadratic polynomial family occurs in Chavan–Stochel, Example 4.5, but there the criterion concerns weak concavity, reducible to a two-by-two log-concavity inequality at later indices. Reza–Zhang classifies complete Hausdorff moment positivity and includes the non-subnormality for complex-root reciprocals. The classical McCullough–Paulsen all-shift Hankel test supplies the method. None of the inspected cited statements implies the newly derived exact three-by-three/all-shift two-hyponormality boundary, its unique cubic root, or its asymptotic constant. Search coverage is finite and does not certify absolute priority.
residual_risks: Historical novelty cannot be certified by finite literature searches; a differently phrased or unindexed finite Hankel classification may exist.
The McCullough–Paulsen full article was not obtained as full primary text; the abstract and its published restatements suffice for the standard criterion.
No external independent proof validation has been performed.

value.rationale: A complete exact 2-hyponormality boundary for the natural quadratic strict 3-isometric weighted-shift model identified in prior literature resolves finite-order positivity that its known weak-concavity and complete-Hausdorff criteria do not. The cubic root describes a nontrivial open range of 2-hyponormal, non-subnormal Cauchy duals, a strictly smaller finite-order threshold than ordinary hyponormality, the rank-defective endpoint, and a sharp universal asymptotic ratio. These are precise and motivated functional-analytic operator distinctions, not merely a numerical slice.
